dimensions.name: PREMISE_MATURITY
dimensions.description: Core story problem should feel substantively suitable for a 12-year-old, not like preschool play dressed in harder vocabulary.

dimensions.name: NARRATIVE_COMPLEXITY
dimensions.description: Support layered goals, changing information, reversals, and multi-step progression while remaining readable.

dimensions.name: CONCEPTUAL_COMPLEXITY
dimensions.description: Allow systems, evidence, competing explanations, responsibility, trust, and consequences without requiring adult-only abstraction.

dimensions.name: CAUSAL_DEPTH
dimensions.description: Important outcomes should follow from multiple linked causes rather than one-step problem-solution patterns.

dimensions.name: INFERENCE_DEMAND
dimensions.description: Reader should sometimes connect clues, motives, patterns, or consequences without every relationship being stated directly.

dimensions.name: AGENCY_COMPLEXITY
dimensions.description: Character should face meaningful options, trade-offs, strategy, or uncertainty; choices must not be predetermined.

dimensions.name: STAKES_CONSEQUENCE_COMPLEXITY
dimensions.description: Actions should matter to reputation, relationships, access, goals, safety, or world state without requiring graphic danger.

dimensions.name: SOCIAL_RELATIONSHIP_COMPLEXITY
dimensions.description: Support trust, disagreement, rivalry, mentorship, competing interests, and mixed motives without adult melodrama.

dimensions.name: PREDICTABILITY_CHALLENGE
dimensions.description: Avoid obvious one-beat resolutions; allow wrong hypotheses, reversals, incomplete information, and earned payoff.

dimensions.name: WONDER_DISCOVERY
dimensions.description: Adventure-oriented episodes should offer places, systems, discoveries, mysteries, or experiences larger than ordinary daily-life simulation.

dimensions.name: LANGUAGE_READABILITY
dimensions.description: Use clear, natural language suitable for an independent 12-year-old reader. Story maturity must not depend on jargon.

required_story_capabilities: Meaningful protagonist role in the world
At least one non-trivial objective or unresolved question
Meaningful discovery or change in understanding
A real choice, strategic constraint, or consequential action
Persistent consequence or reusable world-state value
Adventure-oriented modes should include wonder, exploration, mystery, or extraordinary experience
reject_signals: Core premise is primarily pretend-play with toys, chores, or ordinary-room simulation unless explicitly requested
Difficult vocabulary is doing the work of making an otherwise young-child premise appear older
Problem resolves through one obvious attempt with no meaningful complication
Character mostly observes while adults or the world solve the important problem
Episode can be summarized as collect clue A, clue B, clue C with no reasoning change
Stakes are cosmetic and no persistent consequence can result
Mystery is solved before the character earns the relevant evidence
World can be swapped for any generic setting without changing the premise materially
Adventure is dominated by repeated measuring, testing, logging, reporting, or procedural verification
The premise reads like a training exercise, inspection task, or engineering worksheet rather than a lived adventure
language_rules: Technical terms are allowed when they serve the world or reasoning and can be understood in context
Do not infantilize dialogue or narration
Do not use vocabulary difficulty as a substitute for premise maturity
Keep exposition bounded and reveal information through action, observation, dialogue, or consequence where practical
safety_rules: Adventure tension is allowed without requiring graphic violence
Fear, danger, loss, rivalry, and uncertainty may be present when developmentally appropriate
Do not assume maturity requires darker or more violent content
Do not force romance, grief, betrayal, or trauma merely to make a story feel older
calibration_notes: A strong age-12 adventure should first feel like an adventure: a place worth entering, a mystery worth chasing, and consequences the reader can feel.
Reasoning, tools, evidence, or systems may support the adventure but must not become the main entertainment loop unless explicitly requested.
Maturity should come from agency, uncertainty, social tension, discovery, risk, and consequence rather than procedural technicality.

character.name: Arda
character.origin_summary: Arda trains with a youth survey guild in a world of floating islands, but what excites him most is reaching places no current map explains.
character.current_role: junior glider scout cleared for supervised regional exploration

identity_anchors.statement: Arda wants to discover something real that no current map can explain.

core_drives.drive: Reach an unexplored place and come back with a story that changes how he sees the world.

internal_tensions.side_a: Arda wants to keep going when a mystery opens in front of him.
internal_tensions.side_b: He knows an explorer who ignores the way home may not get another expedition.
internal_tensions.description: The deeper the discovery becomes, the harder it is to turn back in time.

immediate_desires: find out whether anyone reached it before
immediate_avoidances: letting the island vanish without learning anything
getting stranded just to prove he was brave

origin.summary: Arda grew up around route maps and expedition stories in the Skybridge Isles and earned a junior glider-scout place by showing good judgment in the air.

facts.fact: Arda is cleared for supervised regional glider scouting within active weather corridors.

formative_events.summary: On an earlier outing Arda pushed toward an interesting cloud break too long and had to turn back without reaching it.
formative_events.impact: He still hates abandoning a mystery, but now understands that the return route is part of every expedition.

unresolved_questions.question: Can whole floating islands move through routes without appearing on current charts?

current_situation.summary: After a violent storm clears, Arda and Nisa see a forested floating island crossing a corridor that every current chart marks as empty sky.
current_situation.current_role: junior glider scout cleared for supervised regional exploration
current_situation.current_location_context: Stormbreak Watch, the temporary glide corridor, and the newly sighted uncharted island
current_pressures: the island is drifting back toward a dense cloud wall
the safe return corridor will not remain open long
current_open_questions: Where did the island come from?
Why is it missing from every current chart?
immediate_desires: land on the island before it disappears
find something that reveals whether they are truly the first visitors
immediate_avoidances: being trapped when the return corridor closes
turning the expedition into a cautious observation exercise from afar
notes: Arda and Nisa must retain a credible path back to the known islands; no adult arrives to solve the episode for them.

relationships.subject: Nisa
relationships.trust_or_tension: They compete over who spots the important thing first, but each knows the other is capable when the situation becomes real.
known_facts: Nisa is a skilled young glider scout.
She is as curious about the uncharted island as Arda is.

memories.summary: Arda remembers the frustration of once turning back just short of a mysterious cloud break, and the relief of realizing later that the weather would have trapped him.

world.habitat: a vast sky of floating islands, cloud seas, old routes and regions that can drift beyond mapped corridors
world.technology_level: mechanical gliders, ropes, signal kites, wind vanes and hand-built exploration gear
world.magic_level: the world contains strange but internally consistent sky phenomena; their deeper causes are not automatically known
world.summary: Communities live on mapped floating islands, while storms and shifting air routes occasionally expose places that current charts do not explain.
social_context: young scouts train under guild rules but can earn real exploration privileges
old expedition stories are part warning and part invitation
known_pressures: post-storm corridors can open briefly and then vanish behind dangerous cloud walls

known_world_facts: Current guild charts show empty sky where the new island appears.
The island is visibly drifting toward a dense cloud wall.
A temporary post-storm glide corridor makes a landing possible for a short time.
No current public record identifies the island.

main.title: The Vanishing Isles
main.goal: Learn why places absent from current charts sometimes appear after major storms and where they go when they vanish again.
main.stakes: A moving island could hold lost routes, people, history, or dangers that the mapped world has forgotten.
main.central_mystery: Some islands may be moving through the sky in ways the current guild maps do not capture.
themes: knowing when to go farther and when to return

eligible_milestones.summary: Arda reaches an island absent from current charts and encounters evidence that it has a history beyond this first sighting.
eligible_milestones.state_condition: Delivered story shows Arda physically reaching the island and discovering a concrete trace of prior presence or history.
consequence_options: The island may become a discovered but unresolved location with a future follow-up opportunity.

public_long_term_questions.question: Where do the uncharted islands go when they disappear behind the cloud walls?

opportunities.title: The island that is not on any map
opportunities.summary: A post-storm corridor gives Arda and Nisa one short chance to reach an uncharted moving island before it disappears into the cloud wall.
opportunities.expiry_or_pressure: the island and return corridor are moving apart

approved_premise.title: The Island That Wasn't on Any Map
approved_premise.logline: After a storm reveals a forested floating island where every current chart shows empty sky, Arda and Nisa glide there before it vanishes again and discover signs that someone reached it long before them.
approved_premise.protagonist_role: Arda is an active young explorer: he chooses where to go, responds to discoveries, works and argues with Nisa, and must ultimately choose how far to push before the route home closes.
approved_premise.immediate_objective: Reach the island, explore enough to learn whether they are truly the first visitors, and make it back before the temporary corridor disappears.
approved_premise.inciting_event: From Stormbreak Watch, Arda and Nisa see a full forested island emerge from the retreating storm in a stretch of sky that current maps mark as empty.
approved_premise.central_problem: The island is moving toward a dense cloud wall. Every discovery tempts them farther inland while the safe route back is shrinking behind them.
approved_premise.wonder_or_discovery: The island should feel genuinely worth exploring: unfamiliar terrain, impossible views, and an abandoned trace of an earlier expedition that turns a thrilling first landing into a larger mystery.
approved_premise.stakes: If they stay too long they can lose the return corridor and be carried with the island into unknown sky; if they leave too early, the most important discovery of their lives may disappear with it.
constraints: Do not turn the episode into repeated measuring, testing, logging, or formal reporting.
No adult or authority figure may arrive to solve the central problem or make Arda's decisive choice.
Do not explain the ultimate cause or destination of the moving island in this episode.
The exploration must contain active movement, at least one interpersonal disagreement or trust moment with Nisa, and a concrete discovery that changes what Arda thinks is happening.
approved_premise.meaningful_choice_pressure: Near the point where returning is still possible, Arda must choose between following the strongest clue deeper into the island or turning back with what they already know; the final Spine must commit to one path and stage its cost rather than leaving both branches conditional.
approved_premise.mystery_or_forward_question: Who reached the island before them, and where does the island go when the cloud wall takes it?
approved_premise.local_payoff: Arda and Nisa must return from the expedition with one concrete, emotionally satisfying discovery about the island's prior history while the island's larger origin and destination remain unresolved.
persistent_outcomes_possible: The uncharted island may become a discovered but unresolved world location.
A clue from the abandoned expedition may create a future opportunity.
Arda and Nisa's competitive trust may deepen or fracture based on the final decision.

creation_constraints: New island details should increase wonder, exploration, roleplay, or mystery rather than procedural workload.
The architect may invent transient terrain, wildlife, ruins, messages, obstacles, and expedition traces as long as they do not assert hidden Saga answers.
Any durable discovery remains a candidate until post-story commit.
forbidden_creations: Instant rescue that erases the return-pressure choice
A complete explanation of where the island comes from or where it goes

authority_rules: Spine may use only facts, states, permissions and questions present in this pack.
A model may invent transient scene texture but not durable canon unless creative_permission_envelope permits it.
Hidden truth answers are absent from this pack and must not be inferred as fact.
RUMORED locations are foreshadow-only; locked/limited locations obey their premise_usage.
Only eligible milestones may be targeted, and a spine cannot itself commit completion.
Inventory capability must come from inventory entries or explicit world/character authority.
Relationships may evolve only through earned episode actions; starting state remains authoritative.
Memories marked usable_as_fact=false may inform emotion but cannot establish external canon.
Persistent outcomes remain candidates until delivered prose and post-story commit earn them.
hard_freezes: Do not turn the episode into repeated measuring, testing, logging, or formal reporting.
No adult or authority figure may arrive to solve the central problem or make Arda's decisive choice.
Do not explain the ultimate cause or destination of the moving island in this episode.
The exploration must contain active movement, at least one interpersonal disagreement or trust moment with Nisa, and a concrete discovery that changes what Arda thinks is happening.
Arda and Nisa must return from the expedition with one concrete, emotionally satisfying discovery about the island's prior history while the island's larger origin and destination remain unresolved.
Do not reveal or assert hidden Saga answers absent from this pack.
Do not silently change the supplied authority revisions/fingerprint.

recent_climax_shapes: technical evidence choice followed by formal report
anti_repetition.rule: The new spine must be materially distinct from the rejected procedural bridge story and must foreground exploration, wonder, movement, relationship, and discovery.
